title: Acceptance test for reachable configurations
statement: Let $N$ be a finite-state nondeterministic Turing machine over Booleans, let $x$ be a Boolean input, and let $S\in\mathbb{N}$. Suppose there is a function $sp:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ such that every run of $N$ on every Boolean input $y$ under every choice word uses at most $sp(|y|)$ work-tape cells, and suppose $sp(|x|)\le S$. If $C$ is a configuration whose core data and output summary agree with those of some configuration reached by running $N$ from its initial configuration on $x$ under a choice word, then the Boolean indicator of the acceptance-configuration language, evaluated on the encoding of $x$, the code of $C$ at space bound $S$, and $S$, is true exactly when $C$ is halted with output exactly $[\mathrm{true}]$.
hypotheses_covered: N is a finite-state nondeterministic Turing machine over Booleans
There is a function sp bounding space used on every input and choice word by input length
C is reachable up to equality of core data and output summary
